```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(INLA)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# ==============================================================================
# 1. SETUP AND PATHS
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# Set the base path to one leve up from the current path
current_path <- dirname(getwd())

# Set the state abbreviation
state_abb <- "WV"

print(paste("Current Path:", current_path))
```

# ==============================================================================
# 2. LOAD DATA
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# Load SVI TDA Data
tda_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "processed_data", paste0("tda_summaries_2018_", state_abb, "_down.csv"))
svi_tda_data <- read_csv(tda_path, col_types = cols(STCNTY = col_character()))

# Load SMR Data
smr_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "processed_data", paste0("smr_data_2018_", state_abb, ".csv"))
smr_data <- read_csv(smr_path, col_types = cols(FIPS = col_character()))

# Load Geometry Data (GDB)
geo_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "raw_data", "SVI2018_US_county.gdb")
# Note: "layers" in GDB might vary, usually it's the main layer name. 
# You can check layers with: st_layers(geo_path)
geo_data <- st_read(geo_path, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  select(FIPS, ST_ABBR) # Select only relevant columns to match your code
```
# ==============================================================================
# 3. DATA MERGING AND PROCESSING
# ==============================================================================
```{r}
# Merge SMR and TDA data (Left join on FIPS = STCNTY)
combined_data <- smr_data %>%
  left_join(svi_tda_data, by = c("FIPS" = "STCNTY"))

# Merge with Geometry (Left join on FIPS)
# Ensure we convert combined_data to an sf object
combined_data <- geo_data %>%
  right_join(combined_data, by = "FIPS") %>%
  filter(ST_ABBR == state_abb)

# Check shape
print(paste("Shape after adding AL column:", nrow(combined_data), ncol(combined_data)))

```
```{r}
# Cleaning the processed data

# remove rows with zero observed deaths (removing missing data)
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  filter(observed_deaths > 0)


# identify islands (no neighbors) and remove them
nb <- poly2nb(combined_data, row.names = combined_data$FIPS)
islands <- which(card(nb) == 0)
if (length(islands) > 0) { 
  combined_data <- combined_data[-islands, ]
}

# drop rows FIPS starts with ('72', '78', '02', '15', '60')
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  filter(!substr(FIPS, 1, 2) %in% c('72', '78', '02', '15', '60'))


print(paste("Shape after cleaning:", nrow(combined_data)))

```
# ==============================================================================
# 3.5 PROCESSING DATA FOR THE BYM-T MODEL
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# mean standerdize the AL column
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  mutate(AL = scale(EP_POV_AL))
```
# ==============================================================================
# 4. SPATIAL ADJACENCY MATRIX (GRAPH)
# ==============================================================================
```{r}
# INLA requires a graph object or file to define neighbors.
# This replaces libpysal.weights.Queen

# Create neighbor list (Queen contiguity)
nb <- poly2nb(combined_data, queen = TRUE)

# Convert to INLA graph file
nb2INLA("wv.graph", nb)
g <- inla.read.graph("wv.graph")

# Create a unique ID for the spatial random effect (INLA requires integer indices)
combined_data$ID_spatial <- 1:nrow(combined_data)
```

# ==============================================================================
# 5. DEFINE AND RUN INLA MODEL (BYM)
# ==============================================================================
# We use the "bym2" model which is the modern, scaled version of BYM.

# Formula:
# Observed ~ Intercept + Covariates + f(spatial_field) + offset(log(Expected))

```{r}
# C. MATCHING REGRESSION COEFFICIENTS (The "Tight" Priors)
# Python: pm.Normal(0, 1) -> Precision = 1 / 1^2 = 1
# We must tell INLA to use Precision = 1 for Intercept and all Betas
control_fixed_priors <- list(
  mean.intercept = 0, 
  prec.intercept = 1,  # Matches Python intercept sigma=1
  mean = 0, 
  prec = 1             # Matches Python beta_* sigma=1
)

```

```{r}
# Define the new "Uniform/Traditional" priors
#hyper.uniform <- list(
#  prec = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(1, 0.0005)),  # Gamma prior for precision
#  phi = list(prior = "logitbeta", param = c(1, 1))        # Uniform prior for phi
#)

# Run the INLA model with these new priors
#model.uniform <- inla(formula, 
#                      family = "poisson", 
#                      data = data, 
#                      control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
#                      control.family = list(hyper = hyper.uniform)) # Apply here
```




```{r}
formula <- observed_deaths ~ 1 + EP_POV_AV_ORI +
  f(ID_spatial, 
    model = "bym2", 
    graph = g, 
    scale.model = TRUE, 
    constr = TRUE,
    hyper = list(
      phi = list(prior = "logitbeta", param = c(1, 1)),
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01))
    ))

message("Running INLA BYM model...")

# Run the model
# E = expected_deaths is used as the offset (log scale implicitly handled by E argument in family="poisson" 
# or explicitly as offset(log(expected_deaths))). INLA allows `E` argument for Poisson.

model_inla <- inla(formula,
                   family = "poisson",
                   data = combined_data,
                   E = combined_data$expected_deaths, # Assumes column is named 'expected_deaths'
                   control.fixed = control_fixed_priors,
                   control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
                   control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config = TRUE))
```

# ==============================================================================
# 6. MODEL OUTPUT AND DIAGNOSTICS
# ==============================================================================

```{r}

# Print Summary (Fixed effects and Hyperparameters)
summary(model_inla)

# Extract Fixed Effects (Coefficients for Intercept, tda_0, tda_1)
print(model_inla$summary.fixed)

# Extract Hyperparameters (Phi and Precision/Sigma)
print(model_inla$summary.hyperpar)

# Plotting the Spatial Random Field (Structured Component)
# The BYM2 random effect result contains summary.random$ID_spatial
# calculating the mean spatial effect:
combined_data$spatial_mean <- model_inla$summary.random$ID_spatial$mean[1:nrow(combined_data)]

# Simple plot
plot(combined_data["spatial_mean"], main = "Posterior Mean Spatial Random Effect (WV)")
```

```{r}
# Extract Phi Mean
phi_mean <- model_inla$summary.hyperpar["Phi for ID_spatial", "mean"]
print(paste("Mean Phi:", phi_mean))

# Extract Precision Mean
prec_mean <- model_inla$summary.hyperpar["Precision for ID_spatial", "mean"]
print(paste("Mean Precision:", prec_mean))

```
```{r}
# 1. Get the marginal posterior for precision
marg_prec <- model_inla$marginals.hyperpar[["Precision for ID_spatial"]]

# 2. Transform it to Sigma (Standard Deviation = 1/sqrt(Precision))
marg_sigma <- inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/sqrt(x), marg_prec)

# 3. Calculate summary statistics for Sigma
sigma_summary <- inla.zmarginal(marg_sigma, silent = TRUE)

print(paste("Mean Sigma (Spatial SD):", sigma_summary$mean))

```
